intended_object: The ring isomorphism R{X_σ} ≅ R{X_υ} between I-adically restricted multivariate power series rings, induced by a bijection of variable sets e : σ ≃ υ (renaming variables). Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module.
explanation: `adicallyRestrictedSubring I` is the subring of series f with, for every k, only finitely many coefficients outside I^k. That is the standard I-adic restricted condition, here without assuming completeness. The definition restricts Mathlib's `MvPowerSeries.renameEquiv R e`, which sends X_i to X_{e i}, to these subrings. It uses the lemma that renaming along a bijection keeps the restricted condition, since it only permutes coefficient indices. The inverse uses e.symm, and the ring axioms come straight from `renameEquiv`. So it is the natural renaming isomorphism. The setting is a commutative ring R, any ideal and arbitrary variable types, which is fully general. The result could have been stated as an R-algebra isomorphism instead of a ring isomorphism. That is a weaker packaging choice, not an error. Mathlib has no I-adic restricted multivariate power series rings, so there is no direct counterpart. Mathlib only has the underlying `MvPowerSeries.renameEquiv`.
